source.title: What Is The Performance Ceiling of My Classifier? Utilizing Category-Wise Influence Functions for Pareto Frontier Analysis
source.authors: Shahriar Kabir Nahin; Wen-Xiao Xiao; Joshua Liu; Anshuman Chhabra; Hong-Fu Liu

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses influence functions and sample reweighting to improve class-wise accuracy, but does not test the listed generalization claims, including removal of specifically memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on category-wise influence and class-accuracy changes after removing samples, but does not measure random-label memorization, the train–test generalization gap, or the listed optimizer, batch-size, regularization, architecture, size, sharpness, or memorized-example comparisons.
record.test_reason: The study cites Feldman and Zhang (2020), but neither tests nor relies on their memorization-removal finding. Its removal experiments select samples by influence on category-level validation loss, not by their inclusion's effect on predicting their own label. They also lack an equal-size random-removal comparison. The remaining experiments evaluate the proposed reweighting method, without testing V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: category-wise influence vectors assess room for class-wise improvement, and influence-guided sample reweighting can improve target-category performance. The reported practical improvements allow small losses in other categories, so they do not establish strict Pareto improvements in every case.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses category-wise influence estimates and linear-programming-based sample reweighting to improve per-class accuracy; it does not use the original studies' generalization tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The text reports that NLP models on Emotion and AG_News achieved over 90% accuracy across all classes within the first epoch, leaving little room for Pareto improvement; cleaner STL-10 images also generally led to better performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing category-wise beneficial samples decreases target-category accuracy, while removing detrimental samples increases it on CIFAR-10 and Emotion; the text reports similar patterns on STL-10 and AG_News.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Category-wise validation influence predicts the direction of accuracy changes after selected training samples are removed and the classifier is retrained.

fits_no_version.finding: Repeated removal of jointly detrimental synthetic samples improves logistic-regression accuracy; after three iterations the authors report that all label noise has been removed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Iterative removal of jointly detrimental mislabeled samples can improve both classes in this synthetic logistic-regression setting.

record.problems: For the sample-removal results, numerical performance changes are presented in figures and not given in the text. The supplied text reports no uncertainty estimates for these results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results were left out. Reweighting performance-improvement tables were excluded because they test the paper's proposed training method, not a claim version or behavior listed here.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe, including chance-level held-out accuracy for random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Effects of dropout, training-set size, augmentation, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Removal selected by own-label memorization, its test-accuracy cost relative to equal-size random removal, and dataset dependence.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T4 classification conflates using influence estimation with using a listed generalization finding. States here indicate that unlinked rows cannot determine a claim-version effect; they do not negate the study's reported removal effects. No additional result bearing on V1–V8 is present in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning.
Large-batch versus small-batch comparisons under epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.
The removed samples are selected by category-wise influence, not by whether their labels are memorized or by their effect on their own-label prediction.

rows.subject: logistic regression
rows.operation_detail: Removed noisy samples identified as negatively influential for both categories, then retrained.

conditions.value: synthetic linearly separable binary classification with mislabeled samples
samples with negative influence for both classes

rows.measure: Accuracy across both classes; the text says it improves through each iteration and reaches the performance ceiling after three iterations.
rows.value: Accuracy improves with each iteration; after three iterations, all noise has been removed and the model is at the performance ceiling.
rows.note: The supplied text gives no numerical accuracy values for the iterations.
rows.check: The reported improvement after removing jointly detrimental mislabeled samples is accurately paraphrased, but does not measure any claim version. The synthetic label noise is not V1's fixed-random-label experiment.

rows.subject: ResNet-9
rows.operation_detail: Removed the top 10% of beneficial or detrimental samples for each category and retrained; the paper reports the corresponding accuracy changes in figures.

conditions.value: top 10% beneficial samples for a category

rows.measure: Category-wise accuracy change; removing beneficial samples with positive influence leads to a performance drop in the corresponding category.
rows.value: Performance drop in the corresponding category; figure-only magnitude.
rows.note: The text describes the direction, but the values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: The stated category-accuracy decrease is supported by Section 6.1. Selection uses category-wise validation influence, not V8 memorization; no random-removal control is reported. The baseline is retraining with the full training set, although its numerical accuracy is unavailable.
